description.narrative:
Samarbetet är ett 3-årigt stöd för att förbättra Albaniens kemikaliehantering, vilket genomförs av den svenska Kemikalieinspektionen tillsammans med ministeriet för turism och miljö samt andra albanska intressenter. Projektets fokus ligger på närmande av landets lagstiftning till EU-direktiv samt stärkt kompetens och institutionell kapacitet att tillämpa ny lagstiftning och närma sig EU-standarder för en säker kemikaliehantering. Projektet omfattar kemikalier såväl som biocider och växtskyddsmedel och kommer att involvera flera ministerier och institutioner men där ministeriet för turism och miljö är samordnande.
Ett urval av förväntade projektresultat: 1.1 Albansk lagstiftning anpassad till EUs lagar. 2.1 En framtagen plan för institutionell kapacitetsutveckling som är förankrad av relevanta stakeholders/aktörer. 2.2 Ett etablerat kemikaliekontor. 2.4 Relevant personal har ökad kompetens för tillämpning av EUs kemikalielagstiftning. 2.6 En kemikaliehelpdesk etablerad och i funktion. 2.7 Industrin förberedd att genomföra krav i enlighet med EU-lagstiftningen. 3.1 En rapport/studie om införande av nationellt kemikalieregister med rekommendationer för fortsatt arbete. 3.3 Ett funktionellt kemikalieregister.

The cooperation is a three year project support, 2018-2021, to improve Albania's chemicals management implemented by the Swedish Chemicals Agency together with the ministry for tourism and environment and other Albanian stakeholders. The project focus is on aligning Albania's legislation with the EU Acquis and increasing the capacity of the administration to implement the new legislation and get closer to EU-standards for safe chemicals management. The project will encompass work on chemicals, biocides and plant protection products and will involve project staff from several ministries and institutions with the Ministry of Tourism and Environment being the lead institution.
Selected expected outcomes: 1.1 National legislation is further aligned with the EU legislation. 2.1 A plan supporting the institutional capacity building is in place and accepted by relevant stakeholders. 2.2 An established and operational chemicals office. 2.4 Relevant staff are prepared competent authorities tasks under EU chemicals legislation. 2.6 Helpdesk established and in operation. 2.7 Industry prepares for complying with obligations in EU chemicals legislation. 3.1 A report on the chemicals registry outlining the results that can serve as a basis for future work. 3.3 A functioning chemicals registry.

The overall objective is to create conditions, in the area of chemical legislation, for membership in the EU.
The project objective is to have contributed to the effective implementation of the EU acquis on chemicals, biocidal products and PPP (plant protection) at the accession.
Expected outcomes:
1.1 National legislation is further aligned with the EU legislation.
2.1 A plan supporting the institutional capacity building is in place and accepted by relevant stakeholders.
2.2 An established and operational chemicals office.
2.3 Biocidal project risk management system
2.4 Relevant staff are prepared competent authorities tasks under EU chemicals legislation.
2.5 Capacity development of enforcement authorities
2.6 Helpdesk established and in operation.
2.7 Industry prepares for complying with obligations in EU chemicals legislation.
3.1 A report on the chemicals registry outlining the results that can serve as a basis for future work.
3.3 A functioning chemicals registry.

description.narrative:
The project has played a significant role in advancing national legislation, as detailed in Annex 2. These legal acts remain in force until formally repealed and contribute to the overarching goal of establishing conditions for EU membership in the field of chemical legislation. At the same time, they aim to enhance protection of human health and the environment while ensuring the free movement of chemicals and related articles.
Regardng institutional radiness, the Sector of Chemicals has been established and is fully operational. Its capacity to assume the role as competent authority has been developed through training and on the job support. A chemicals helpdesk has been set up and provided with written and hands on recommendations as to structure and operations. The chemicals management team at the Ministry of Environment has also received similar support. Additionally, a cross-sectoral Chemical Safety Committee and a Biocidal Product Commission, responsible for authorizing biocidal products, have been created and are functioning effectively. Experts from Albanian institutions involved in biocidal products have received training thhrough thhe project.
The involvement of Albanian institutions in the project has strengthened national capacities, improving practices for preventive chemical control and supporting the long-term implementation of chemical legislation. Training activities have also enhanced enforcement capabilities as staff at the Market surveillance Inspectorate have also received extensive training and the inspectors manual developed under the project will remain available for continued use.
Furthermore, the project has facilitated the participation of Albanian organizations in international forums on chemicals management, including the International Conference on Chemicals Management and meetings under the Basel, Rotterdam, and Stockholm Conventions.
All of this has contributed to the overarching goal of institutional and legal readiness for EU accession
The project has not fully delivered on the component on establishment of a register of chemicals, which also resulted in the project not using up its entire project budget. The establishment of a chemicals register in Albania required cooperation with the Albanian e-agency AKSHI, which became a bottleneck for this part of the project.
Concerning harmonization of legislation there are also some results n ot fully achieved; towards the end of the project KemI assisted MoE in including the latest updates on REACH and CLP. Lawyers from KemI provided a table of concordance with notes on what new articles needed to be included. These changes are yet to be formally included in legislation and adopted. The project intended to assist on alignment of biocidal legislation with little success. This legislation is under the responsibility of ministry of health which further complicated communication.
The project has supported the preparation and update of the national plan for chemicals, which if adopted would fulfill requirements of Law 27/2016 on how institutions should work together on chemicals. The slowness in adoption of the plan caused the first version to become obsolete before even adopted, a second revised version was finalized shortly before the end of the activity period and is yet to be adopted.
In the common position EU invites Albania to align with EU legislation such as reach, CLP, PIC, POP, Biocides, Asbestos, Merucy. The need to allocate more resources to inspection and enforcement is underlined.
The EU country report of 2025 states that "The REACH implementing legislation on the registration, evaluation, authorisation and restriction of chemicals still needs to be adopted and adequate administrative structures to be set up. The same applies to alignment with Biocides Regulation."
This assessment indicates that even if the project formally complied with the planned results in component 1, it has not fully achieved harmonization with the EU Chemicals acquis.
The activities targeted to industry are limited to activities of the helpdesk and a seminar on PFAS in foam.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
